---
title: "Harness architecture"
---

`gtskill` is a thin orchestrator around the [Claude Agent SDK](https://pypi.org/project/claude-agent-sdk/).
Everything the harness does can be summarized in one sentence: **given a
CSV and a natural-language prompt, mount exactly one skill into an
ephemeral `.claude/` directory, launch an agent with a bounded tool set,
and capture what it produces.**

This chapter unpacks that sentence.

## The run model

Every invocation of the harness — from the CLI or from an evaluation
sweep — resolves to a single **`RunSpec`**. Given a `RunSpec`, the
`runner.orchestrate` module builds a **run directory** on disk, loops
over the selected prompts and repeats, and hands each individual
invocation to `runner.engine.run()`, which is the *only* place that
touches the Agent SDK.

```
RunSpec  ──►  orchestrate.run_spec()  ──►  engine.run()  ──►  Claude Agent SDK
                    │                          │
                    │                          └─► one ephemeral .claude/
                    │                              one transcript.json
                    │                              one table.py + table.png
                    │
                    └─► one run directory on disk
                        with per-prompt subdirs and aggregate summary
```

## `RunSpec`

`runner.spec.RunSpec` is a dataclass. It is the *only* input the runner
takes:

```python
@dataclass
class RunSpec:
    skill: str                    # "prose" | "scripts" | "creator" | "house"
    prompts: list[PromptRef]      # each = (prompt text, data CSV path)
    repeats: int = 1              # with-skill invocations per prompt
    model: str = "haiku"          # shortcut label OR raw Claude model id
    baseline: bool | None = None  # None = auto (on iff repeats > 1)
```

Everything in the harness that used to be a separate runner
(`consistency_runner`, `test_runner`, `skill_creator_runner`) is now
folded into this one shape. A **single** prompt is a `RunSpec` with one
`PromptRef` and `repeats=1`. A **convergence** study is the same thing
with `repeats=3` (or more). A **sweep** is a `RunSpec` with many
`PromptRefs`. Nothing else changes.

Every `RunSpec` is validated up front (via `RunSpec.validate()`) before
any Chrome is launched or any API call is made, so bad paths and empty
prompt lists fail cheaply.

## Orchestrate

`runner.orchestrate.run_spec()` is the single driver both the CLI (via
`run.py`) and any programmatic caller go through. It owns the run
directory, one shared sidecar Chrome for the whole run, and the
per-prompt loop.

### The run directory

Every run writes exactly one tree under `runs/<type>/`, where `type` is
one of `single`, `convergence`, or `sweep`:

```
runs/<type>/<timestamp>_<skill>_<slug>/
  run.json               # RunSpec + resolved config + status + timings
  summary.json           # aggregate pass/fail + tokens/cost across prompts
  .chrome-profile/       # sidecar Chrome's isolated profile, removed on exit
  prompts/
    <prompt-name>/
      convergence.json   # only when repeats > 1
      contact_sheet.png  # only when repeats > 1
      baseline/          # only when baseline is enabled
        table.py
        table.png
        transcript.json
        data/                # symlinked CSV — never copied
        .claude/             # ephemeral, mounted skill root (empty for baseline)
      repeat_1/ ... repeat_N/
        (same layout as baseline/)
```

The CSV stays where it is: the agent reads from a **symlink** in the
run dir. It is never asked to copy data around.

### Per-prompt loop

For each `PromptRef` in the spec, `orchestrate` runs `repeats`
with-skill invocations and, if `baseline` is enabled, one baseline
invocation with `variant="none"` — the agent sees no `.claude/` at all.
`baseline` is `None`-by-default and resolves to `on` iff `repeats > 1`,
so a convergence study automatically produces the no-skill control it
needs to lift-adjust the with-skill scores.

## Engine

`runner.engine.run()` is the choke point. It:

1. Builds `run_dir/.claude/` from scratch, mounting exactly one skill
   (see below).
2. Constructs `ClaudeAgentOptions` with a restricted tool set
   (`Read`, `Write`, `Edit`, `Bash`, `Glob`, `Grep`) and a permission
   gate that logs Write/Edit calls but generally allows them within
   the run directory.
3. Calls `claude_agent_sdk.query()` with the prompt and the mounted
   skill root, streaming the message trace to `transcript.json`.
4. Executes the resulting `table.py` in a subprocess against the venv
   Python — the script itself renders `table.png` via
   `gt.gtsave("table.png")` attached to the sidecar Chrome (see
   below).

## Sandboxing and per-run isolation

The harness enforces isolation on three axes.

### One skill per run

`_prepare_skill_root()` **rebuilds** `run_dir/.claude` on every
invocation with `rmtree + recreate`, so there is no way for a previous
run — with a different skill variant, or a stale baseline — to leak
into the current one. Only the source skill for the selected variant is
copied under `run_dir/.claude/skills/`. Baseline mounts *nothing* —
`skills=[]` is passed to the SDK.

### One run directory per invocation

Every prompt invocation gets its own subdirectory. Writes are scoped
there; the agent never touches the repo tree it was launched from.
Data CSVs are symlinked in read-only from `data/` under the repo root.

### One sidecar Chrome per run

On macOS the Claude Code sandbox blocks the mach services Chrome
touches during launch, so the agent's sandboxed Python cannot start
Chrome itself. Instead, `orchestrate` launches **one** headless
`nokap.Chrome` in the parent process at the start of the run and
threads its CDP websocket URL to the agent via
`GTSKILL_CHROME_WS`. `gt.gtsave()` picks that up from a venv `.pth`
startup hook (installed by `_ensure_sidecar_hook()` on first use) and
attaches, rather than trying to spawn Chrome from inside the sandbox.

The sidecar's profile lives under `run_dir/.chrome-profile/` and is
removed on teardown, so a run leaves no state on disk beyond the
tracked artifacts.

## Sidecar Chrome and CDP rendering

The rendering path in one flow:

```
agent (sandbox)
    │
    │  writes table.py
    │  runs table.py via Bash tool
    ▼
subprocess: python table.py
    │
    │  imports great_tables
    │  imports _gtskill_sidecar (via .pth hook)
    │  reads GTSKILL_CHROME_WS
    │  attaches to sidecar over loopback CDP
    ▼
gt.gtsave("table.png")   ──► CDP screenshot ──► table.png on disk
```

The `.pth` hook (`gtskill_sidecar.py`) is installed once per venv per
run into the venv's site-packages. It patches `great_tables`'s Chrome
startup to attach to the already-running sidecar instead of launching
a new one. Every run tears down its own hook copy so subsequent runs
against a different sidecar can't cross-connect.

## What the harness *doesn't* do

- **It does not restart Chrome per prompt.** One sidecar covers a whole
  run (many prompts, many repeats), so a sweep pays the Chrome
  startup cost exactly once.
- **It does not judge with the same model that wrote the table.** The
  judge (`runner.judge`) runs a separate model (`sonnet` by default,
  overridable via `GTSKILL_JUDGE_MODEL`) and never sees the writer's
  transcript.
- **It does not silently retry.** If the agent's script fails, the
  transcript is preserved and the invocation is marked `fail` in
  `summary.json`. The runner does not swallow errors to make its
  reports look cleaner.
